subject: Shiny crash on EC2 with cryptic message: "Operation not allowed without an active reactive context."

messages.author: 10c48bb8d9cd5f59
messages.subject: Shiny crash on EC2 with cryptic message: "Operation not allowed without an active reactive context."
parts:
I have a simple Shiny app that reads a mysql table and displays a graph of aggregated data.  the app works fine on a local Mac (I use a tunnel to enable RMySQL to connect to MySql DB running on EC2)

Next step - I used Shiny AMI to spin an EC2 micro instance, put mysql on it so I am able to do tunnel through mysql socket to the real MySQL server running on another EC2 instance (same setup as on my local Mac that works)

Next step - I test that mysql connection through tunnel is working in R by running an R shell on EC micro with Shiny and running the same R commands as in my Shiny App: establish connection, do a select on a table using dbSendQuery. Everything works fine, just like on a local machine (I use Mac)

Now the fun part, I go to Shiny URL in the browser to  point to the shiny on EC2 instance.  Application starts ok and connects to MySQL (I know because when I had misconfigured tunnel it gave me error messages at this point).  However, when I try to click on something that would trigger a select it hangs for a while and then crashes.  When I go to Shiny log on the server I see the following cryptic error message:

Listening on port 51279
Warning in mysqlExecStatement(conn, statement, ...) :
  RS-DBI driver warning: (unrecognized MySQL field type 7 in column 38 imported as character)
Warning in mysqlExecStatement(conn, statement, ...) :
  RS-DBI driver warning: (unrecognized MySQL field type 7 in column 39 imported as character)
Warning in mysqlExecStatement(conn, statement, ...) :
  RS-DBI driver warning: (unrecognized MySQL field type 7 in column 1 imported as character)
Warning in mysqlExecStatement(conn, statement, ...) :
  RS-DBI driver warning: (unrecognized MySQL field type 7 in column 4 imported as character)
Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext() : 
  Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive function.)
Calls: runApp ... $ -> $.reactivevalues -> <Anonymous> -> <Anonymous>
Execution halted



As you can see by the warnings it was able to do a select, however I am not sure at which point and why it crashed.  Any ideas are appreciated. This error is reproducible and occurs every time.  Table is about 10k rows so should have no memory issues

kind regards,
- Ilya

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Shiny crash on EC2 with cryptic message: "Operation not allowed without an active reactive context."
parts:
That error happens when you access a reactive object outside of a reactive context like renderText(), reactive(), and observe(). For example, the input values are reactive. This is ok:

shinyServer(input, output) {
  output$txt <- renderText({ input$num })
}


But accessing input$num outside of the renderText() will result in that error:

shinyServer(input, output) {
  input$num
}


The same is true if you try to access a reactive expression outside of a reactive context.

-Winston

Hi Winston,

I don't see anything like this in my code (which is very simple and shown below), in addition the same code works fine from my iMac, so unless it is a version of Shiny or EC2 issue I don't see how the same code produces this error on Linux but not on MacOS

server.R:

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
   
  all.objects <- read_object_data_from_db()
   
  lastDate <- all.objects$accounts$created[nrow(all.objects$accounts)]
  
  # Return the requested dataset
  datasetInput <- reactive({
    
    switch(input$dataset,
           "accounts" = all.objects$accounts,
           "datapoints" = all.objects$datapoints)
  })
  
   
  output$growthChart <-  renderPlot({
    n <- as.integer(input$aggDays)
    dates <- seq(from=lastDate - 7*input$lookbackWeeks, to=lastDate, by=n)
    
    objectCountsByDate <- data.frame(dates=dates,
                                     counts=sapply(dates, createdBefore, datasetInput()))
    
    p <- generateGrowthCharts(objectCountsByDate, "Accounts")

messages.subject: Re: Shiny crash on EC2 with cryptic message: "Operation not allowed without an active reactive context."
parts:
A quick thought - do you have an old version of Shiny installed on the Linux server? The old versions required syntax like this:
  reactive(function() { ... })
whereas more recent versions of shiny use this:
  reactive({ ... })

I'd suggest running sessionInfo() on both machines to make sure everything is the same version.

-Winston

That was indeed the problem.  The public AMI I used had a different shiny version, but the error message is very cryptic....

thanks for the idea!

- Ilya

On Tuesday, June 25, 2013 10:38:46 AM UTC-7, Winston Chang wrote:
A quick thought - do you have an old version of Shiny installed on the Linux server? The old versions required syntax like this:
  reactive(function() { ... })
whereas more recent versions of shiny use this:
  reactive({ ... })

I'd suggest running sessionInfo() on both machines to make sure everything is the same version.

-Winston



On Tue, Jun 25, 2013 at 1:24 AM, Ilya Li <ilip...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Joe,

Sorry I was out camping for 4 days.  I have simplified code to pin point the error, here is the server.R code that works on Mac but produces the same error on Linux EC2 micro instance:

library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  
  # Return the requested dataset
  datasetInput <- reactive({
    
    switch(input$dataset,
           "accounts" = 1,
           "datapoints" = 2)
  })
  
})

And I am sure that is the same code running.  I removed all references to DB or anything else so it is pure Shiny framework that is doing something weird on Linux apparently.  It draws the correct UI first and immediately displays the dialog error: 
"The application unexpectedly exited.
Diagnostic information has been dumped to the JavaScript error console."

Here is the contents of the log error file:
Listening on port 39418
Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext() : 
  Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive function.)
Calls: runApp ... $ -> $.reactivevalues -> <Anonymous> -> <Anonymous>
Execution halted

- Ilya

On Thursday, June 20, 2013 1:01:27 PM UTC-7, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
You're absolutely positive no code differs between your local computer and EC2? Even read_object_data_from_db (and you're sure that doesn't access any reactives, either directly or indirectly?)?

How about changing the line

all.objects <- read_object_data_from_db()

to

all.objects <- isolate(read_object_data_from_db())

Does that change the error?



On Thu, Jun 20, 2013 at 12:42 AM, Ilya Li <ilip...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Winston,

I don't see anything like this in my code (which is very simple and shown below), in addition the same code works fine from my iMac, so unless it is a version of Shiny or EC2 issue I don't see how the same code produces this error on Linux but not on MacOS

server.R:

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
   
  all.objects <- read_object_data_from_db()
   
  lastDate <- all.objects$accounts$created[nrow(all.objects$accounts)]
  
  # Return the requested dataset
  datasetInput <- reactive({
    
    switch(input$dataset,
           "accounts" = all.objects$accounts,
           "datapoints" = all.objects$datapoints)
  })
  
   
  output$growthChart <-  renderPlot({
    n <- as.integer(input$aggDays)
    dates <- seq(from=lastDate - 7*input$lookbackWeeks, to=lastDate, by=n)
    
    objectCountsByDate <- data.frame(dates=dates,
                                     counts=sapply(dates, createdBefore, datasetInput()))
    
    p <- generateGrowthCharts(objectCountsByDate, "Accounts")
     print(p)

  })
})

On Wednesday, June 19, 2013 8:05:29 AM UTC-7, Winston Chang wrote:
That error happens when you access a reactive object outside of a reactive context like renderText(), reactive(), and observe(). For example, the input values are reactive. This is ok:

shinyServer(input, output) {
  output$txt <- renderText({ input$num })
}


But accessing input$num outside of the renderText() will result in that error:

shinyServer(input, output) {
  input$num
}


The same is true if you try to access a reactive expression outside of a reactive context.

-Winston





On Wed, Jun 19, 2013 at 3:02 AM, Ilya Li <ilip...@gmail.com> wrote:
I have a simple Shiny app that reads a mysql table and displays a graph of aggregated data.  the app works fine on a local Mac (I use a tunnel to enable RMySQL to connect to MySql DB running on EC2)

Next step - I used Shiny AMI to spin an EC2 micro instance, put mysql on it so I am able to do tunnel through mysql socket to the real MySQL server running on another EC2 instance (same setup as on my local Mac that works)

Next step - I test that mysql connection through tunnel is working in R by running an R shell on EC micro with Shiny and running the same R commands as in my Shiny App: establish connection, do a select on a table using dbSendQuery. Everything works fine, just like on a local machine (I use Mac)

Now the fun part, I go to Shiny URL in the browser to  point to the shiny on EC2 instance.  Application starts ok and connects to MySQL (I know because when I had misconfigured tunnel it gave me error messages at this point).  However, when I try to click on something that would trigger a select it hangs for a while and then crashes.  When I go to Shiny log on the server I see the following cryptic error message:

Listening on port 51279
Warning in mysqlExecStatement(conn, statement, ...) :
  RS-DBI driver warning: (unrecognized MySQL field type 7 in column 38 imported as character)
Warning in mysqlExecStatement(conn, statement, ...) :
  RS-DBI driver warning: (unrecognized MySQL field type 7 in column 39 imported as character)
Warning in mysqlExecStatement(conn, statement, ...) :
  RS-DBI driver warning: (unrecognized MySQL field type 7 in column 1 imported as character)
Warning in mysqlExecStatement(conn, statement, ...) :
  RS-DBI driver warning: (unrecognized MySQL field type 7 in column 4 imported as character)
Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext() : 
  Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive function.)
Calls: runApp ... $ -> $.reactivevalues -> <Anonymous> -> <Anonymous>
Execution halted



As you can see by the warnings it was able to do a select, however I am not sure at which point and why it crashed.  Any ideas are appreciated. This error is reproducible and occurs every time.  Table is about 10k rows so should have no memory issues

kind regards,
- Ilya

sudo npm install -g shiny-...@0.3.6

KD
